[34mInvestigated:[0m The format rules for m:ss and h:mm:ss timer strings. The existing parseCompound helper and its undefined-versus-throw convention. The Node test suite, typecheck, and Biome lint and format results after the change.

[33mLearned:[0m New helpers use an undefined-return convention, so parseClock returns undefined for invalid input and never throws. parseCompound still throws TypeError, and the parseCompound JSDoc says so. In m:ss the leading minutes field accepts any number of digits, so 90:00 is valid. Seconds, and minutes in h:mm:ss, must be two digits from 00 to 59. Negatives, fractional seconds, surrounding whitespace, and one-digit seconds all return undefined.

[32mCompleted:[0m parseClock is implemented and exported from src/index.ts. parseClock('1:30') returns 90000 and parseClock('01:02:03') returns 3723000. Its tests are in src/parse-clock.test.ts.
